lines.text: This case contrasts a right-anchored image with an ordinary inline image of the same source and width.
The anchored image must retain its aspect ratio while nearby text wraps around its left edge.
ANCHOR START — the image belongs at the right edge beside the following prose.
W RAP 01 START — This sentence is deliberately long enough to occupy several lines. W hile those lines
are beside the logo, their right edge must stop before the image and preserve the authored ten-point gap.
W RAP 02 START — Text that reaches below the anchored logo must return to the full body width without
retaining a false right indent. The circle remains on the left side of the image and the striped rectangle
remains on the right. — W RAP 02 END.
ANCHOR END — no wrapped text may overlap the image, disappear behind it, or remain narrowed after
INLINE CONTROL START — the next copy is an ordinary flow image and must consume its own vertical
space instead of allowing text beside it.
INLINE CONTROL END — this line must begin below the control image at the full body width.
PASS: the anchored logo is right aligned with square text wrapping and preserved aspect ratio; the inline
control occupies an ordinary full-width flow row.
